text_fidelity_a:
ThinkFun Zingo Sight Words Award Winning Early Reading Game for Pre-K to 2nd Grade - Toy of the Year Finalist, A Fun and Educational Game Developed by Educators for Boys and Girls, Multicolor My boys are 3, 5, and 7(almost 8), and they all enjoy this game. As a bonus, it requires NO batteries!

Both the game boards and the game pieces have both pictures and words on them. Your child doesn't have to be able to read to play the game, but it does make the picture/word connection, to an extent. The game goes so fast that even I tend to mostly just look at the picture, and ignore the words. There is still a slight connection, though, and every little bit helps when a little one is learning words.

The game comes with 7 game boards. These are double sided. The green side is for a less competitive game, and better for the littlest ones. There aren't that many shared pictures on this side, and the players aren't in so much of a rush to grab the tiles. The red side has a bit more competition, since there are more pictures in common. The players have to rush to grab a matching tile, before someone else grabs it.

Each game goes really quick, so you're not spending a ton of time on each game. There are a few different options for playing the game. You can go the traditional "Bingo" route, or you can match designs, play multiple cards, or even fill up the whole card, which is what my oldest prefers. The traditional route is just way too quick for my children's tastes.

Their favorite part of the game is the Zinger. It's super easy to load the tiles, and then slide them into view. They have to take turns sliding the tiles into view, because it's so much fun. The only negative we've seen is the fact that sometimes it seems the same tile is being played over and over(in a row). When you first open the box, you'll have to mix these tiles up, since they are placed together matched. If you don't mix them up, you WILL have the same tile continue to show up in a row. Even then, it sometimes happens that the same one will keep showing up. It is easy to dump them out, mix them up, and then reload them, though.

This is a super simple game, but so much fun for little ones! I even enjoy playing it with them, which is pretty important.
text_fidelity_b: ThinkFun Zingo Sight Words Award Winning Early Reading Game for Pre-K to 2nd Grade - Toy of the Year Finalist, A Fun and Educational Game Developed by Educators for Boys and Girls, Multicolor

Plug the battery in when it is level so that the gyros are initialized correctly.

text_fidelity_a:
My Little Pony Equestria Girls Pinkie Pie Doll For the past few months, every trip we made to the big-box store involved a determined march through the toy section, looking to see if the Equestria Girls dolls were yet available. My 9 year old, who watched My Little Pony endlessly, and has already watched Equestria Girls more times that I want to count, was thrilled when the dolls were finally available! Her favorite doll, by far, is the Deluxe version of Rainbow Dash [[ASIN:B00CANI9RQ My Little Pony Equestria Girls Rainbow Dash Hairstyling Doll]] -- because of all that multi-colored hair. I think Pinkie Pie comes in a close second place -- again, because of all that hair. The other Equestria Girl dolls have smooth, straight hair, so Pinkie Pie's masses of pink curls are a little different and fun to play with. And her pink skin tone is a little less eerie than the purple and blue of some of the other dolls.

Pinkamena Diane Pie has sparkly eyeshadow and a "cutie mark" on her cheek, reflective of her virtue. Pinkie Pie's cutie mark consists of three balloons, and reflects her virtue of laughter. Her happy, chaotic spirit is reflected in her curly hair. There's not much in the way of accessories -- a plastic headband to tame all those curls, and a little pink hairbrush. There is only one item of clothing -- the skirt -- so I don't think that these dolls will be dressed and undressed much -- that real appeal is the hair. The boots are interchangeable, so we have switched the boots around on several of the dolls. I find the boots a little disturbing -- well actually the legs, because the doll legs end at the ankle, and the boots pop on to the ankle. Without the boots, the dolls are footless. Kind of creepy, but I guess it's better than having those teeny weeny little Barbie high heels all over the place. Pinkie Pie has a small hole in her upper back -- it's pretty well hidden under all of that hair -- but some of the other dolls come with butterfly (or angel??) wings that pop into the hole, so Pinkie Pie can borrow those wings if she's so inclined, since she too has a hole for attaching the wings. Each Equestria Girl doll also comes with a sheet of stickers and a little pamphlet -- but my daughter hasn't even looked at those, and I expect they'll end up in the trash soon. The long piece of hair is supposed to be the horse-tail, but it is odd that it has a different texture than the rest of Pinkie Pie's hair. As a mom, I thought that the hair could have been better done -- the plugs are sparse and separated, so if you don't pull Pinkie Pie's hair back just right, she looks like she just visited Hair Plugs for Men -- not pretty.

Pinkie Pie is a cute doll with a big pouf of brushable hair. Is she super high quality? Probably not. Will she be a cherished heirloom to pass down over the years? Who knows. But is she a fun plaything for an Equestria Girls fan? You bet.
text_fidelity_b: My Little Pony Equestria Girls Pinkie Pie Doll

Also, we play it simpler, without the "nope" chip, meaning we don't have to worry about anyone taking our deck (or ending up with someone else's we don't want). text_fidelity_a:
ELEGOO Building Block Car Kit, Intelligent and Educational Building Block Toy Car Robot Kit 3 in 1 for Fun and STEM Learning Toy This review was written by my 11 year old son, Nathaniel.

----------

I’m an avid LEGO builder, and I’ve participated in the FIRST LEGO League as well as LEGO robotics competitions. I’ve built kits at home as large as 1000 pieces. But although some of these had moving parts, like wheels, doors, gears and suspension, I’ve never built a fully robotic kit that I owned myself. Besides, LEGO robotics is way too expensive for a kid like me… So, for a long time serious robot-making felt like an impossible goal. But then imagine my surprise when I got my first Elegoo kit!

The Elegoo kit: The Elegoo Building Block Car Kit is an attractive package and comes in a neat and reclosable plastic container. I really liked the container design as it wouldn’t rip as easily as the standard LEGO kit cardboard box would. All the parts are bagged by type. There are MANY connectors in the box as well as wheels. This is not an official LEGO kit, so all of the parts are LEGO clones, however, they fit just as well as the official product. The robotics-specific parts are nonstandard LEGOs, however they have similar connections to a normal LEGO and have magnets that snap them to one another. The kit has a large flat paper instruction sheet that folds out to cover an entire table. It's large enough to literally build the entire project on. However, it only contains startup instructions for the project. You’ll need to visit an android or ios app store to download the “Colego app” in order to find building instructions and the programming tools for the car.

The Colego app (co-LEGO?): This is where things go downhill. The user interface is so-so, so I will split it into 3 parts: The manual, the coding, and the coding lessons.

In the manual the part colors aren’t always accurate so there is some confusion during assembly. For instance, a gray part shown in the manual is actually black in real life. You also can’t zoom into small spaces, making examining details difficult. Also, a suggestion, double-tapping on a part should zoom in on it to show you how many studs or technic holes it has. This will definitely help with differentiating parts.

In the coding section of the app some elements take up almost the whole screen so you can’t edit your code. There is just not enough space at all. You also can’t change what the blocks are auto-set to when they first pop up. There is no redo, undo, copy or paste (for example the SCRATCH coding app has all these features). This makes it very hard to make long code strings. Also the blocks don’t fully fit together in the user interface leaving gaps. This doesn’t affect your code, but looks very sloppy. Basically, the coding interface and layout is the absolute worst I’ve seen for any robotics kit. It needs to be fixed. Other issues I have with the app are that there is only one “when start button pressed” block and the bluetooth power saving settings are pretty aggressive and turn off the connections very quickly. As far as the robotics hardware goes, most of it is pretty well built, but I think the ultrasonic sensor is not the best. They are rather closely set together and seem to get confused by many typical household objects (like my mother’s sneakers).

Lastly there are the coding lessons. They aren’t bad, but they go by type (movement, sound, etc). You can’t see the next type of lesson or skip/scroll through lessons you’ve already done. This is a good kit for kids who have done complex LEGO kit building and know how to plug things in using cables and ports, but are new to programming. Especially if they will only make very simple programs as the user interface of the app falls apart with larger blocks of code. Arduino use or knowledge would also help but if you’re already using Arduino this kit will be too simple for you.

Good overall and I had fun with it, but not a real LEGO Robotics replacement. If it worked with Buzzwizz or BrickController 2 it would be a LOT more useful. But it is not recognized by those apps. The most fun I'm having with it is using it like a little remote control car with the app's control function on the home page under kit.
text_fidelity_b: ELEGOO Building Block Car Kit, Intelligent and Educational Building Block Toy Car Robot Kit 3 in 1 for Fun and STEM Learning Toy

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

The packaging indicated Callie is from Japan, and she definitely has more almond-shaped eyes than Meredith. Her light skin, brown hair (instead of black), and eye shape reminded my bi-racial girls of themselves. That is the true gift of doll lines that have unique face sculpts, to provide a mirror so all little girls can have a doll that resembles them, as well as a truly diverse line of dolls.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie

For the target audience of 2 yrs and above (most likely 2-4 yr old will find this interesting for a while), the use of primary colors, very simple mechanical parts (just two 'doors' that can be easily maneuvered by a 2 yr old) and the relative size will prove to be attractive. text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz Make sure you know what you are getting yourself into before purchasing this item. I think it is a great item for the right person/people. If you are the type of person who likes participating in an escape room, or think you might like to participate in an escape room, then this might be for you. But this is not a game of chance. There is no luck. You do not roll the dice, or pick a card. You must complete each task before continuing. You either get the task right, or wrong. If you get it wrong, then there are hints to help, if you choose to use them.

It takes about 2 hours to complete. It could take you more time if you don’t use the hints, and perhaps less time if you do use the hints. It’s played with between one and 6 players. Honestly, I think 6 players would be too many. If you had 6, I think four would be playing the game and two would be making sure the drinks and snacks keep flowing. ;-)

Once you complete this game, you will not play it again, because you already know how to complete all of the tasks. But you certainly could give it to friends who have not played it. Or, perhaps you could invite other friends over who had not played it before and you could assist them with it.

Once you remove the lid, you will find the different pieces. But do NOT open the box that is inside until you are given instructions to do so. There are tasks which must be completed before you open the box that is inside.

If you want to have an idea of how to get started, then I highly recommend that you do an online search for “Unfiltered Gamer Break In Alcatraz”. These are a couple of guys who will walk you through about the first 20 minutes. If you don’t want to go that far then you can simply watch until they have completed the 1st task so you know exactly what you need to do. Yes, this can be a little complicated, but if you at least watch them complete the 1st task, you’ll know how to get started.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz

text_fidelity_a: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set I absolutely love this swingset. We ordered it from Costco, because the price was a bit lower. WB Games Lego Marvel's Avengers - Playstation Vita Compared to other Vita Lego games, it is disappointing. Those who played other games on consoles are probably happy, since it sounds closer to a console in terms of content, but, honestly, it is disappointing, and a bit broken.

First of all, I hate the city hub. It is too big. While it does come into play a bit during the main gameplay, having to navigate it during cleanup is a pain. Trying to find all the collectibles that are scattered throughout the city is annoying, even with a guide. Half of them are in such obscure places that you would never think to look for them there, let alone be able to see them from the distance (if they even render if you just pass by). The missions in the city are just painful; while the smash challenges are easy enough but rely more on luck than anything, the ground and jumping time trials are manageable, but the flying ones are utterly impossible. Precision flying controls with constant change in altitude are ridiculously broken, particularly when you can't see where you are supposed to go. I easily plat any other Vita Lego games, as they are easy and relaxing. And in this game, I have everything else done, but these flying challenges, I just give up on them.

Speaking of the trophies, several of them are glitched; even if you complete everything they still do not show up. And the game is glitched too; I had to restart the game at least twice because it froze and I could not move at all.

The main mission was on the shorter side. Apparently, the console had extra missions about Cap 2 and Thor movies. Rather than having Manhattan hub, I honestly would have preferred a few extra levels. Also, they did have many cutscenes from the movies, but they cut out the punchlines of most of those scenes, which was also pretty disappointing,

This is supposed to be a rock, paper, scissors game, and each toy has a rotating plate that you can pick red, blue, or green. But, you'll end up spending more time trying to make it work, than actually playing.

My Megatron arrived broken, and I would guess from the shape of the other three toys, that one of your toys will be broken. I would have returned it for a replacement, but I was pretty sure that every set would have a broken Transformer.

It also has an online game. This is the worst type of online game, because it's highly addictive, it encourages you to buy more toys just so you can get higher levels in the game, but the game isn't fun and it's not very educational. The online game is also a glorified rock, paper, scissors game. If you don't want begging kids, have them stay away from the online game. You get four coupons that give you one online robot each.

Pros:
+It's an officially-licensed Transformers product.

Cons:
-My Megatron arrived broken, and I would guess from the shape of the other three toys, that you'll get about 1 out of every 4 of these toys that are broken.
-The toys transformed too quickly. They're supposed to wait until they hit something.
-The plates that change color on each toy was totally stuck on two of them
-No matter how you dress up rock, paper, scissors, it's really not that fun of a game.
-The pieces that aren't already broken will probably break after only a few uses.

Munchkin® Draw™ Bath Crayons Toddler Bath Toy, 5 Pack OK...so here's the deal with these...
5 stars for how much my 17mo old son LOVES them.
3 stars for how the crayon is constantly coming out of the plastic holder.
Averages to...4 stars.
No one is really addressing a few things, so I will...
these are super bright, amazing, soft crayons that are each a very distinct & different color.
In our particular tub, they color perfectly...but we have a somewhat "satin" finish as opposed to the shiny white finish which is what I imagine is the problem for people who say they don't work. I notice they color fantastically on dry or "damp" tub surfaces...but not as well on truly wet, slick surfaces.
We have a clear silicone table mat with a scene silkscreened on that I sometimes wet the back of and slap on the tub wall so he can color away on it like a coloring book page. Again, the crayons work perfectly when the surface is dry or damp, but can't get grippy enough for the color to stick when it's slick wet.

These crayons do constantly come out of the holders but I just keep pushing them back in. They also push back into the holder because the button is where my son grips the crayons in his tiny hands but when that happens he just moves on to another one, since there are 5.

I put these in to a bag of goodies I gave him for Valentine's Day and ours are still going strong with daily...prolific...color & scribble use on the tub, his tub toys, his picture mat, himself, and Mommy....head to toe. He does lots of "body art" with these, and he enjoys using his scrubby sponge for clean up and erasing his handywork, as much as he does the coloring part!

To me...these babies are worth their weight in gold if you have a budding artist on your hands, the right kind of tub surface, and teach the little virtuoso how to scrub it all clean to start with a fresh canvas! We LOVE...and I mean...LOVE them, and I can't see us ever being without them as my son is pretty much obsessed with all things artistic, and where he is allowed to just cut loose & get messy. These are perfect!

P.S. if you are concerned that teaching them to color on surfaces is a bad or confusing message, which makes perfect sense...I'd say that this is the way to let them be creative & have a blast but teach them that coloring on wall is only for the bathtub and only with these crayons....a concept they will need to learn.

I would recommend getting your first set somewhere that you can return them if they don't work on your tub. Also, get a matte finish silicone baking mat, or matte silicone placemat...wet the back, stick to wall & let them color on that. It works great for us!

Takenoko Board Game | Bamboo Farming Game | Panda Themed Strategy Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 8+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Matagot We had the pleasure of playing this in our most recent game night, and it was delightful. You start with a few "quests" based on bamboo for pandas to eat, bamboo in the "fields", and the arrangement of those "field" tiles (as well as access to water ...). It's actually rather simple. Each turn you get to expand the game by adding field tiles (up adding water or other upgrades to the tiles), grow bamboo, have the panda eat the bamboo, or take on more "quests". As everything but the bamboo the panda eats belongs to everyone, there's a passive cooperation, and other than the score at the end (based on completing those cards), it doesn't feel that competitive. If another player lays down irrigation, that's not irrigation that solely benefits them or takes away from what you have, rather it adds to what you have and may well help complete one of your quests. We played with folks from 7 years old on up, and everyone had a great time.

The only real negative (and I don't see the need to deduct any stars from the rating) is that this is at max a four player game. I could'd imagine playing with less than 3, and 4 really is the sweet spot.

It doesn't break unless really forced to. The sprinkles and charm are nice editions and my daughter was surprised that the paper straw released readily from the slime.
The big oversight is that all of the imagery shows off the fun of combining the two colors together. The first problem that causes is one of storage. The two colors come separately packed in small containers with no extra room. This means if you combine them, you have no where to store the combined slime. Also, this should be fairly obvious, but as soon as you start mixing the colors it takes about 5 seconds for the red and white to simply become a pink. You could make the swirl shown in the product photos, but you'd never be able to interact with it without forever just having a pink slime.

Lastly, while the packaging is probably more eco-friendly than most, it is super non-descript. Just a brown box with a couple of tube and a small baggy of sprinkles and the charm.

Stemnex Amazing Steam Engine I would recommend this one more for older children and teenagers because there is over 100 parts here and it may be a bit too challenging for younger kids. Regardless, this is one of the neatest things ever. Kids who love trains will definitely love this. I am reminded of something my dad helped me build for a science fair project when I was in 4th grade, and I won a blue ribbon. The one I had though was made from metal parts and springs and such that he put together from old carburators and such. It looked very much like this one. Working on this made me think of my dad when we built my science project. So this would be perfect, in my honest opinion, for any parents to work on with their kids. You just might make some cool memories. It may also be a good item for kids who are home-schooled and learning about this kind of thing in science.

As for product attributes, the pieces go together easily and the instructions are pretty easy to follow. I recommend possibly not taking the pieces off of the brackets until they are needed, this way they won't get lost. The box is quite large, but just the right size to store away under a bed or raised sofa.

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) I'm just combining my thoughts on the various guns and products into one review, in case anyone would like to do a bit of comparing in one spot.

Darts:

The darts are kind of like a third of a straw, with a cool rubber-like tip. These tips ONLY stick to the special targets, which are on the shields(both the wearable ones and the ones that attach to the guns). There are also targets that stick to the wall. (I just taped the top of these targets, as opposed to sticking the whole thing on the wall.) We tested these out on mirrors and windows. They really don't stick to anything, but the special targets.

They're mostly bright colored, which makes it easier to find them once they've been shot. You'll have to take several time outs just to gather darts.

This company has made it perfectly clear that these darts are NOT made for little ones. I just want to reinforce that. I have an 18 month old that puts things in his mouth constantly. We found a large rock in his poo diaper. :S These are simply irresistible to him with their chewy rubber tip. He's chewed the tops off a few of them, even when we were trying to keep a close eye on him. The tops DO come off when chewed on, so these are definitely a choking hazard for little ones.

I try to teach our boys to never aim a gun at anyone, but I've been hit with a few of the darts. One hurt, but the others didn't. I think it depends on how close the gun is, and simply how the dart hits a person. In general, they don't seem to hurt too much.

Other than chewing, they seem pretty sturdy, though. They're had lots of use and bending, but they still work in the guns.

Farshot Blaster:

This is the smallest gun in this line(that we have...there seems to be a smaller "clipfire"). You pull back the top to "pump it up". It will only hold 1 dart at a time for shooting, but 2 spares fit in the bottom of the gun.

This gun is the easiest to aim, as far as target practice, and if that's what you'd like it for, I'd recommend this one. I've found it to be a great stress reliever. When the little ones are creating chaos, I can pull out this gun, tape a target to the wall, and do a little target practice.

Twisted Spinner Blaster:

This is the medium sized gun in this line. To shoot it, you pull an arm on the gun back towards yourself. The darts are loaded in the round end. It will hold 8 darts. As with all the guns, it comes with removable shields.

This one is a little harder to aim, but it's still fun.

Rapid Madness Blaster:

This is the largest gun in this line. You push and pull an arm to pump it up. The trigger is super sensitive, so it takes a couple of seconds to shoot all 20 darts that it holds. Those darts are held in a clip that slides into the side of the gun. This one is the most fun, BUT you don't get much shooting time before having to round up darts.

Bandolier:

This is an adjustable strap that you can wear across your body. It has a special target that the darts will stick to. It will also hold 12 extra darts.

Eye goggles:

These are pretty cool. As advertised, they won't fog up. They're made of a thick-like plastic/rubber, and give you "bug vision". They're also adjustable. My little ones are younger than the recommended age, but the clip kept coming off with them, and we put the goggles back together so much that I wanted to throw them away. Still, I don't think adults will have that problem, and they really are pretty cool!

Targets:

These are a little smaller than I prefer, but they do come in slightly different sizes and shapes. You get different points for different areas. The darts DO stick really well to these targets, and ONLY these targets, but if the dart hits wrong, it still won't stick. I'd say our darts stuck about half the time with the larger guns, and about 3/4th of the time with the farshot blaster. You can peel the back off and it will stick to the wall/door, but as I mentioned above, I just taped it instead. They're a fun way to create a little "battle" zone in one's room, or just simple target practice.

Overall, we've had tons of fun with these guns, and just think they're all pretty awesome.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

Paw Patrol, Transforming PAW Patroller with Dual Vehicle Launchers, Ryder Action Figure and ATV Toy Car, Kids Toys for Ages 3 and Up Pros:

My son loves Paw Patrol and he loves Chase. He hasn't put this toy down since the moment we gave it to him. It's high quality, quite detailed, and actually much larger than we thought it would be. Even though Chase is relatively small, you can still see and appreciate his features quite clearly.

The launcher aspect is great. It's not fancy, but it does send chase shooting out which has been a source of fun for hours for my kid. Both vehicles are usable separately, so it's like having two toys in one.

Cons:

The projectiles seem a little small - if you have a kid who likes to put things in his mouth, then I would put these parts away. They're not necessary to really enjoy the toy, and they'd probably just get lost in the first 30 minutes anyway.

As with any toy that has flashing lights and sounds, this can get annoying, especially because it is a siren after all. Parents who can't deal with that can just take the the batteries from the get-go.

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll Mattel is always creating a new hair fun Barbie doll, as they know girls love to style, set, color and sometimes even cut their doll's hair. This new Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll offers fun with hair coloring- only in an array of pastel rainbow colors. The doll comes with a color cartridge that includes a row of 5 colors- pink, orange, green, blue and purple. You simply load the hair cartridge into the hair tool and slowly and firmly swipe it onto Barbie's hair where you want the rainbow of colors. The colors come out very pastel looking with the exception of the blue and purple- they are darker. Make sure you do this on an old towel- as it is an inky dye mess, until Barbie's hair has dried from the dye.

Once the rainbow dye has dried, our girls adored braiding the colored hair, and using the hair clips and hair bands to get some really colorful looking hair styles. When the fun wears off from that coloring and they want to re-color a different part of Barbie's hair- get out a bottle of white vinegar and an old towel. You will want to pour some vinegar in a bowl and put the doll's hair that is colored in the bowl, until the color comes out. If you have a problem with the darker purple color like we did, you will want to make a paste of baking soda and vinegar in the bowl and put it on the hair. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes, then take her to the sink and rinse. The color usually all comes out within 5 minutes, but if yours isn't- do it again. When the color is all gone- wash with a dab of shampoo- towel blot dry, brush straight, then let sit until the hair is completely dry. Now you're ready to color again.

This Rainbow Hair Barbie is quite a stiff mannequin- no bendable legs- but she is jointed at the arms, legs and neck. One arm is permanently bent- the other straight. She does have cute hoop earrings, a bracelet, heels, brush, hair accessories and a colorful dress. She is pretty much a stiff mannequin doll that loves to go to the beauty salon for her rainbow streaked hair. This can be fun if you have an old towel and vinegar, so the dye will come out easily for the next coloring. I only wish Mattel would tell you that you will need a towel for the mess and vinegar to easily remove the dye- I only knew the way to easily remove the dye from being a dry-cleaning inspector years ago. The hair coloring is fun, but it would have been nice if she had bendable legs for all the sitting this 4 Star doll will be doing at the hair salon.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll

The insert in the box comes in a wide variety of languages, the pieces come inside the sturdy box wrapped in a bag. Its quality throughout.

text_fidelity_a:
Rio Grande Games Stone Age [[VIDEOID:9645a95d436279cab83d9584b2798107]] In this video, I show one round of playing the game. The game is fast paced, and it's about an interesting time in human history.

This is a pretty fun game, but for me it got old really fast. I really like empire building games, like [[ASIN:B002L6HJCI Age of Empires]], so I thought I would love this. But, I just liked it, I didn't love it.

The problem is that there's really only one strategy to the game, which is this: Get as many civilization cards as you can, and try to spend 100% of your resources by the time the game ends.

Pros:
+If you love the stone age, then this is probably a pretty good game for you.
+It's a pretty fun game.
+If you have a group of super casual gamers, you'll probably enjoy this for a long time. But all it takes is one serious gamer to disrupt the game for everyone.
+The game goes by pretty quick, and gets quicker the more you've played it.

Cons:
-Scoring is a little confusing. You typically score about 200-350 points on a game, but the score only goes to 100.
-Limited strategies, since there really is only one strategy
-Not enough luck to make it fun for casual gamers
-I wish they would have play tested this game a little bit more. I got the feeling that if they would have changed a few things on the cards and scoring, it would have been an awesome game. For example, civilization cards are way too heavily weighted.
text_fidelity_b: Rio Grande Games Stone Age

Owning this unit has renewed my desire and my love for the hobby and I'm looking forward to continuing exploring further with my hs700d great Job Holy Stone!

text_fidelity_a:
Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud This is a completely different kind of game and the idea of stars and lanterns is abstract. It says it is easy to learn, but to be honest, don't bring your friends together to learn the game. You should set it up, read through the directions and pretend to have two friends with you to understand what is going on. THEN you can explain the game to your friends. The reason is because you can tell this game was not designed in America, there are a few minor English mistakes. The directions have interesting choice of words. So I'm going to try my best by using parentheses to show the words they used in the directions.

The goal of the game is when a word card is revealed, you try to figure out which dixit (picture) cards match that word--by the picture itself, the color(s), inspiration, characters, etc. Then you mark an X (cross) for each dixit card you feel matches that word. At the same time, you want to choose cards you think your friends will choose. If your friends chose that card too, both of you earn stars (sparks) and so on. If they didn't, then you lose (fall) and stop there. If you marked X for too many dixit cards (hoping to get a lot of points), more likely your friends won't have that same card marked and that will make you lose. You have to work like a team, trying to figure out what your friends will choose and win. (This is what they mean by the word, greedy.) This is a good way to teach kids how to perceive the pictures and THINK of others and what they could be thinking, again a "teamwork." This is where it is supposed to be fun. My daughter liked it, but my son didn't like it.

I have one suggestion for you as parents or caregiver of a child age 8 or over. (Ages for the game is for 8+.) I suggest you form the first few turns, you handpick the words you feel your child will be able to "match" then go from there. You handpicking and seeing a few cards in advance honestly does not change the game. The game actually entirely relies on the other players' dixit card choices.

There is one rule that seems pointless. Of course you need to read the directions first to understand what I"m talking about. Here I go anyway--suppose you "fall" then at the end of the game when everyone is ready to score. If you have some sparks and a super-spark from one of your dixit cards that you marked off (crosses), you wipe away one star (but not the super-spark star) then count the remaining stars (sparks). The super-spark star has the same point value as the other sparks so I'm not sure why it makes a difference to wipe off a star or a super-spark star.

This game is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. It's also created in China and I don't know that it's going to be that great, at least for some U.S. audiences.
text_fidelity_b: Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud

As a die hard Star Wars Fan this Saber has a lot going for it, but a few cons. First the build and look are nice. The sound is also very good. The price is one of the best reasons for getting one. As of today a 40% off coupon making it around $72.00. To me at this price point shows you how much Disney and Star Wars The Black Series is ripping people off.

For the $72.00 you're getting 12 Light Sabers "colors" compare that to $250.00 and higher for one color. Now for the cons the blade is held in place by three set screws and it still has a bit of a lose feeling not much but its there. The other thing is the control button it is a bit cumbersome and by that I mean the holding down or pushing or doing the fast twist while holding button down to change sound fonts. I know some other saber makers use similar features but not this hard to change. One of the sound fonts is not even from Star Wars. I did not know what it was and could not stand it, but you might like. The problem was it took me several tries to change it and it should not be that hard to change.

So even with those two minor faults, this is still a great Saber for the price. As someone who was 10 years old when Star Wars came out, even now holding this and turning it on makes me smile.

"May the Force be with You"

text_fidelity_a: T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle T. S. Shure had a temporary design lapse with this product; probably, the worst coming out of this brand.  Excellent idea coupled with poor execution only increases the frustration one would feel about the product.  The idea of 'magnetic' pieces to help discover countries and continents is great; so is the use of some cutesy imagery that often is often ascribed to a particular country (the dragon shaped like the Great Wall of China is a clear standout).  But trying to cramp all kinds of information in a tiny board proved disastrous.  The pieces are cut with no logic - the sub-continent looks from another planet; the font size for the capitals is so tiny, the target audience will barely notice it;  there are random airplanes and ships distracting the overall map and adding no value.  The tiny pieces are clearly not to be allowed anywhere near babies (it is rated for 6-15 years, to be fair; though it will be a miracle if anyone in that age group will use this for more than a day).  On the positive, with the weak magnetic pull and cardboard-feeling tiny pieces are bound to be lost sooner or later. And then you could create a new game - "which country is missing?".  That may be a better use of this playboard;
text_fidelity_b: T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle
